intro: An empirical CDF answers how much observed mass lies at or below a threshold. Ties create jumps that must be counted inclusively.
task: Return the fraction of sample observations less than or equal to each query threshold.
requirements: samples and queries are nonempty vectors. Samples need not be sorted and repeated observations carry repeated mass.
For each query q, return count(samples<=q)/len(samples). Preserve query shape and order.
Use the right-continuous convention: every observation exactly equal to a query counts toward its probability.

Use real finite numeric inputs with magnitude at most 1e6, excluding booleans. Vectors have length 1..128 and matrix axes have length 1..128 unless a tighter bound is stated. Leave all inputs unchanged; raise ValueError for invalid inputs.

hints.title: Find the structure
hints.body: Sorting observations makes each threshold a boundary between included and excluded samples.

hints.title: Build the calculation
hints.body: Use the insertion point after equal values so tied observations are all counted at the query.

explanation: Each sample contributes mass 1/n. The empirical CDF adds those masses up through a threshold and therefore includes every tied value at that threshold.
Sorting once permits binary-search queries. The result is a step function rather than the interpolation used by the earlier quantile exercise.
